verdicts.reasoning_critique: heaviest_resources lists the two cover.gif files at 5442 KB and 1440 KB, and page_weight_kb is 7365. 'Improve image delivery' (6,652 KiB) and 'Avoid enormous network payloads' back this up. Replacing animated GIFs with MP4/WebM or static WebP is the standard, effective fix. One caveat: the LCP element is text, so the GIFs inflate total load rather than LCP, but the issue only claims 'delaying load', which holds.
verdicts.priority_critique: This is by far the biggest problem in the report: about 90% of page weight, with no field data to show users are unaffected. High is right.

But top_issues gives only 300 ms of savings and never says which requests block rendering, so blaming render-blocking for the whole delay overstates the evidence. The fix also names the Google Tag Manager script as something to re-strategize. That script appears only under heaviest_resources (176 KB), not as a render-blocking resource, so treating it as a cause of delayed rendering is invented.
